title: Khadijah, first believer
hook: the angel brings a message for one woman alone: greetings of peace from her Lord (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ali's words: a brother in faith, or an equal in creation. Your line was words from Ali. Who did you try the letter on? Today a new stretch begins: the mothers of the believers. Day eight hundred seven.

Peace, from her Lord. In a report preserved by Bukhari, the angel Jibril says to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him: here is Khadijah, coming to you with a vessel of food. When she reaches you, give her greetings of peace from her Lord, and from me. A message from heaven, addressed to one person by name, about to arrive with her hands full. The Qur'an calls the Prophet's wives mothers of the believers. Today the first of them: Khadijah.
screen: `SHE COMES WITH A VESSEL OF FOOD.` → `JIBRIL NAMES HER.` → `PEACE FROM HER LORD.`

segments.voice: First, the title of this stretch. Surah thirty-three, verse six, in Pickthall: "The Prophet is closer to the believers than their selves, and his wives are (as) their mothers." So for the next days we meet them one at a time. Why is Khadijah greeted like this? Go back to the night everything began. Bukhari's account of the first revelation has the Prophet coming home from the cave of Hira shaking, saying: cover me, cover me. He tells Khadijah he fears for himself. And she answers him, not with a theory, but with a list of what she has watched him do. Never, she says. By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep the ties of family. You carry the burden of the weak. You give to those who have nothing. You honor your guest. You stand by people when trouble comes. Then she takes him to her cousin Waraqah, who knew the earlier scriptures, to hear what it might mean. Tradition remembers her as the first to believe him. Notice how she believed: by trusting the character she knew, when he himself was afraid. And notice how she was remembered. Aisha says in Bukhari that she never felt jealous of any woman the way she did of Khadijah, though she never saw her, because the Prophet spoke of her so often, and would send gifts to her friends. Then the greeting itself. In the same report, Jibril adds glad news: a house in Paradise for her, made of hollow pearl, with no noise in it and no weariness. The one who steadied him in a frightening night is promised a place of quiet. Greeted by her Lord.
screen: `HIS WIVES ARE AS THEIR MOTHERS.` · `COVER ME: HE COMES HOME SHAKING.` · `SHE LISTS WHAT SHE HAS SEEN HIM DO.` · `A HOUSE WITH NO NOISE.` · then, large: `GREETED BY HER LORD.`

segments.voice: The practice: honor someone faithful. Settle, and let your breath slow. Bring to mind one person who has stayed steady with you, or with someone you love, through a hard stretch. Do what Khadijah did: make a short list. One thing you have seen them do. A second. A third. Hold each one for a breath. If you pray, you can ask peace for them by name. If not, simply let the list stand, and notice who is on it. The bell holds the time.
Khadijah. The Prophet's wife, the one who steadied him on the night of the first revelation, and the one Jibril greeted with peace from her Lord. Today's word.
Your line: greeted by her lord. Today, tell one faithful person one thing you've seen them do. Out loud, or in a message. Day eight hundred seven.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Khadijah among the mothers of the believers, and her words on the night of the first revelation, from Sahih al-Bukhari, are often retold when the beginning of the revelation is taught.

fork.setup: your husband comes home shaking, saying he fears for himself after something in the cave. what do you do?
options: tell him to keep it secret and rest.
remind him of the good he does, then take him to someone who knows the scriptures.
go to the cave yourself to see what happened.
fork.reveal: in Bukhari she says Allah will never disgrace him, lists his kindness to kin, the weak, the poor and guests, and takes him to Waraqah.

original.note: Arabic: her name, as the hadith of the greeting gives it.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Prophet's first wife, a name from the early story.
what it means: the one who steadied him by trusting his character, and was greeted with peace from her Lord.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari 3 for her words on the night of revelation; Bukhari 3820 for the greeting and the house of hollow pearl; Bukhari 3818 for Aisha's jealousy.
